{"description":"One JWT-SVID bearing two audiences gives both relying parties the same sub,
which is a cross-consumer correlation handle. SPEC-HIRE.md:83 says a consumer
'cannot correlate with any other consumer's identifier' and PRFAQ.md:16 repeats
the guarantee; SPEC-HIRE.md:94 says presenting a specific audience triggers
derivation of that consumer's pseudonym.

NOW LIVE. This bead was filed saying "NOT LIVE: hire-grpc/src/service.rs signs
claim.spiffe_id(), not a pseudonym, so no pseudonym is being leaked today."
That premise is FALSE as of 2026-09-15. Pseudonym derivation has landed:

  hire-grpc/src/service.rs:420   .pseudonymous_id(claim.spiffe_id(), &consumer)
  hire-grpc/src/service.rs:417   "is no branch here that can emit claim.spiffe_id().uri()"

and a live daemon confirms it -- a token fetched on this machine carried
sub = spiffe://ssh.local/pseudonym/56f19c5c... rather than the root identity.
So the condition the bead said to wait for has already happened.

THE REAL QUESTION IS A DIVERGENCE, and it is a trust-model call, not a bug fix:
the code derives the pseudonym from the CONSUMER (the attested socket peer, its
executable hash), while SPEC-HIRE.md:94 describes it as derived per AUDIENCE.
Those disagree whenever one consumer names two audiences:

  code today  one consumer, one pseudonym, one sub, both audiences see it
  spec text   each audience gets that audience's own pseudonym

Under the code's model, two relying parties named in one token can correlate
the user at that consumer. Under the spec's model they cannot, but a single
JWT cannot carry two sub values, so multi-audience would have to collapse to
one audience per request -- which collides with the settled rule that
'repeated string audience' is normative (proto/spiffe/workload/workload.proto:
117-118) and that presence folds strictest-wins across EVERY audience.

Decide which of consumer-scoped or audience-scoped pseudonyms is intended
before writing code; the answer changes the SPEC's normative text either way.
"}
